description: A lynx grown through with crystal. Light bends wrong around it, and its tail-blade sings when it strikes.
lore: [[characters/646b922c|Sigrun]] heard one before she saw it and put a hand out to stop the person walking next to her, which is not a thing she does. The tail-blade sings on the strike, one high note, the same note every time. In her trade that sound means a flaw running all the way through, and an edge that is going to let go, and the only open question is on which stroke. She stood in the trees a long while listening to an animal make the noise a bad blade makes, and could not manage to dislike it.

The crystal comes up at the shoulders, the hips and the brow, and it is still coming. It sits heaviest on the joints, the worst place on an animal to put weight, so an old one moves like something much older than it is. You can find the rubbing rocks out in the crystal country: a smooth boulder with a scatter of snapped points around the base. That is grooming. It is trying to get something off itself that is itself. The same growth bends the light, so what you see stands a hand's width from where the lynx is, always to the same side, and hunters are taught to strike beside the animal and trust the correction over their own eyes. The ones who cannot make themselves do it come back saying it moved. It did not move. There is no account of one ever moving at that moment.
gm_notes: Sigrun's craft carries the record: the singing note is the sound of a failing edge, so the one person qualified to hear it hears something on its way out. The rubbing rocks are the sad physical detail (grooming at a thing that is itself) and a findable landmark. Ends on the aiming rule rather than a summary, and the refraction offset is fixed and learnable, so it can become a real combat mechanic later.
